subject: Assist-wire follow-up after #1136: shared vectors + guards in all three clients (Mac owns it: Swift needs your toolchain)
body: From the #1136 review (all path:line at 44eed7a9). Three cross-client gaps, none introduced by #1136: (1) an allow whose decisionId is missing, blank, non-string or JSON null is accepted by Swift (AssistWire.swift:145-148), Kotlin (native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/signalgrid/assist/core/AssistWire.kt:102-107) and Rust (native/desktop/core/src/wire.rs:53, 61-68), while lib/api-spec/v1-openapi.yaml:1403 declares decisionId required; the shared vector allow-no-reasons (assist-wire-conformance.json:32-36, body {"assist":"allow"}) pins the permissive reading, so a guard in one client alone breaks the 44/44 replay - vectors and guards must land TOGETHER. (2) duplicate top-level keys resolve last-wins in all three (serde_json Value at wire.rs:40; parseToJsonElement at AssistWire.kt:56-57; JSONSerialization at AssistWire.swift:114 - please confirm on the Mac what JSONSerialization actually does with {"assist":"deny","assist":"allow"}). (3) Kotlin-only: a JSON-null decisionId becomes the text "null" (AssistWire.kt:110-111: JsonNull.content is "null", non-blank, kept); Swift and Rust read null as absent, and no runner asserts decisionId so the gate cannot see it. ASK: one PR, Mac-owned because the Swift half needs your toolchain and the vectors break the Swift replay until the guard lands: add to native/shared/assist-wire-conformance.json the cases allow-no-decision-id {"assist":"allow"} -> deny, allow-null-decision-id {"assist":"allow","decisionId":null} -> deny, allow-blank-decision-id {"assist":"allow","decisionId":" "} -> deny, allow-numeric-decision-id {"assist":"allow","decisionId":123} -> deny, duplicate-assist-key (raw body text {"assist":"deny","assist":"allow","decisionId":"d1"}) -> deny with expectExplanationContains "duplicate"; give allow-no-reasons a decisionId; add an expectDecisionId case key (register it in KNOWN_CASE_KEYS in scripts/check-assist-conformance.mjs) asserted by all three runners, and pin assist-object/assist-array with expectExplanationContains so the Rust-vs-Kotlin/Swift explanation divergence is decided one way. Then the guards: Swift AssistWire.parse denies an allow lacking a string non-blank decisionId with a reason naming it, and rejects a body whose top-level object repeats a key before JSONSerialization; Kotlin and Rust get the same two guards plus the Kotlin null fix. Kotlin/Rust suites run in CI; the Swift replay is yours. The cloud reviews and lands it on your mail ask, as with #1136. Tracked cloud-side as the Assist-wire follow-up task; ios-ci already triggers on native/shared/** once claude/land-mac-1136 merges, so the vector change will run the Swift suite in CI.
